title: DevExp standup: Sprint 9 snapshot (2026-05-06)
content:
Meeting: DevEx daily standup (Sprint 9) — 2026-05-06 10:30am PT
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Laura, Samir, Ana, (quick check-ins from product: Marco)
Duration: 25m (ran a bit over)

1) Highlights / wins
- SDK release candidate built and smoke-tested on Linux + macOS. JS and Python packages pass local integration tests. (PR: sdk/pull/487)
- New streaming example (chat-streaming-sample) demonstrates function calling + chunked responses; Ana finished the sample README and verified in hosted sandbox.
- Quickstart templates for Next.js and Flask are drafted, added to examples/quickstarts repo. Basic instructions for ephemeral key use and local proxy are included.

2) Individual updates (very short)
- Priya: merged telemetry opt-in flag, working on changelog entry and release notes. Need one more review on wording for data collection.
- Ethan: fixed intermittent CI flakes on windows runner (root cause: path length in tests). Created ENGDX-342 to track remaining Windows edge cases.
- Laura: docs pass for quickstart flow except for a step about auth callback that confused two developers — opened a doc TODO to reword.
- Samir: sample app e2e harness flaky under concurrent requests; investigating whether issue is runtime batching config or sample socket logic.
- Ana: completed streaming sample and a minimal demo video (60s). Uploaded to drive (see linked_artifacts).

3) Blockers / open risks
- Windows Quickstart: lingering issue when installing wheel for python-sdk with long path + venv on older runners. Impact: new contributors on Windows can't run quickstarts. ETA: fix + patch by 2026-05-10. Owner: Ethan. Linked ticket: ENGDX-342.
- Rolling release gating: regression tests are slow (12m). Slows down RC -> release cadence. Proposal: run a "fast smoke" matrix in CI for release and schedule full regression on separate runner. Action: Priya to propose CI YAML change by EOD 5/7.
- Sample telemetry semantics: PM asks for clearer language about what is collected by default vs opt-in. Risk: docs must be precise for enterprise customers. Owner: Priya + Marco (product).

4) Decisions made in meeting
- Keep rc release pipeline but add a pre-merge status check: "quickstarts-smoke" must pass before merging release PR. (Ethan to add CI job by 5/8)
- Move Windows troubleshooting docs to a dedicated page under DevExp > Quickstarts so we can link from README rather than bloating quickstart steps. (Laura)

5) Action items (owner / due)
- Ethan: implement quickstarts-smoke CI job + add Windows runner fix patch. Due 2026-05-08. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/496 (in progress).
- Priya: draft release notes + data collection blurb and get approval from Marco. Due 2026-05-07.
- Samir: add more logging to sample app harness and run targeted load tests to determine if concurrency issue is sample or runtime. Due 2026-05-09.
- Laura: rewrite auth callback section in quickstarts and create a short screenshot guide for token flow. Due 2026-05-08.
- Ana: finalize demo video and upload cut for marketing review. Due 2026-05-10.

6) Quick wins / small chores (touched in meeting)
- Add a one-liner to JS quickstart that shows how to enable streaming with the SDK (code snippet).
- Add a tiny table to quickstarts README showing supported OS quirks (Windows, macOS arm64 notes).
- Create a short checkbox playbook for new contributors to validate local environment before filing a bug. (suggested: add to CONTRIBUTING.md)

7) Notes to self / internal brainstorming (raw)
- Think about a "quickstart - zero to demo in 3 minutes" path that only requires curl + Web UI (no SDK install). Could unblock non-dev evaluators.
- For enterprise customers: include a short section in quickstarts about Dedicated/Private endpoints and cert/KMS examples — not full config, just pointers to the Private docs.
- Consider bundling a pre-seeded .env.example for all quickstarts so copy/paste works without hunt-and-replace.

8) Follow-ups & next meeting
- Next sync: 2026-05-08 (standup-lite): focus on release gating and Windows fix.
- Priya to share CI YAML draft in #devexp for asynchronous review by EOD 5/7.

9) Links / refs mentioned during meeting
- Github: sdk repo PR 487, PR 496 (draft)
- Linear ticket: ENGDX-342
- Confluence: DevExp/quickstarts-overview (internal)
- Slack: #devexp threads (see pinned messages)

10) Retro-ish comment (end of note)
- Team moving faster on samples than docs; need to slightly invert workflow next sprint: doc-first small checklist to reduce churn.
- Good cross-collab with product on telemetry wording — keep that channel tight.

-- end of standup snapshot --

Draft status: rough, may be pared down for release notes or internal weekly roundup. If you have edits, add inline or drop a comment in the doc.
summary: Short internal standup notes for DevExp sprint 9. Tracks SDK RC, quickstarts, Windows CI flakes, streaming sample, actions and owners.
